quiz.q: Thin-airfoil lift slope is…
quiz.why: c_l = 2πα.

quiz.q: Aspect ratio is…
quiz.why: Span squared over area.

quiz.q: At maximum L/D…
quiz.why: Minimizing C_D/C_L gives KC_L² = C_D0.

quiz.q: A higher aspect ratio mainly reduces…
quiz.why: K = 1/(πeAR).

quiz.q: More angle of attack always means more lift.
quiz.why: Past the stall angle the flow separates and lift drops.

quiz.q: Symmetric airfoils cannot lift.
quiz.why: They lift at a positive angle of attack.

quiz.q: Wingtip devices make induced drag zero.
quiz.why: They reduce it; only an infinitely long wing would have none.

quiz.q: Thin-airfoil theory: find c_l at α = 5°.
Find the aspect ratio of a wing with span 11 m and area 16.2 m².
Using c_l = 2πα, what angle gives c_l = 0.5? Give your answer in °.
For the Example 4.3 airplane, find C_D at C_L = 0.36.
If AR rises from 7.5 to 15 (same e and C_D0), how does (L/D)max change?
quiz.why: K halves, so (L/D)max grows by √2 to ≈ 19.4.

quiz.q: 4.92 per rad ≈ 0.086 per degree, 22% below the 2D value.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit. Find the lift slope of a wing with AR = 8 and e = 0.9.
This is stated in the unit. With C_D0 = 0.025, e = 0.8 and AR = 7.5, find (L/D)max and the C_L where it occurs.

quiz.q: Long, slender wings are one of the most direct ways to cut fuel burn, because induced drag falls as aspect ratio rises. That is exactly the “efficient aircraft technology” path in NASA’s sustainable-aviation work.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: The albatross, which glides for hours over the ocean, uses the same physics: a long, thin wing with a high lift-to-drag ratio.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: An airfoil is a wing’s cross-section. Camber lets it lift at zero angle of attack; thickness adds strength and room for fuel.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: Thin-airfoil theory predicts a lift slope of 2π per radian (about 0.11 per degree) until the flow separates and the wing stalls.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: A finite wing loses lift slope to its tip vortices: a = a₀/(1 + a₀/(πeAR)), with aspect ratio AR = b²/S.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: Total drag C_D = C_D0 + KC_L² with K = 1/(πeAR). Maximum L/D occurs where induced drag equals parasite drag.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.
